title: So and such, too and enough
subtitle: so/such ... that, and talking about more or less than is needed

blocks.text: Both **so ... that** and **such ... that** are used to show the results of a situation or action.

rows.use: with an adjective: so + adjective + that
rows.example: Al is **so good that** he was made manager.

rows.use: with a noun: so + many/much + noun + that
rows.example: Al sells **so many cars that** he was made manager.
Al is **such a good worker that** he was made manager.
Al gets **such good results that** he was made manager.

rows.use: such + a lot of + noun + that
rows.example: Al makes **such a lot of money for the company that** he was made manager.

rows.use: with an adverb: so + adverb + that
rows.example: Al works **so well that** he was made manager.

blocks.text: Both **too** and **enough** are used to talk about how much or how little of something there is. We use **too** to describe the negative effect of having more than necessary. We use **enough** to describe the effects of having/not having the right amount of something.

rows.use: with an adjective: too + adjective (+ full infinitive)
rows.example: It's **too cold** to work in the garden.
Carol isn't **patient enough** to work as a teacher.

rows.use: with a noun: too + many/much + noun (+ full infinitive)
rows.example: Jonty works **too many hours** to have any hobbies.
We don't have **enough money** to pay our bills.

rows.use: with an adverb: too + adverb (+ full infinitive)
rows.example: I got there **too late** to see the manager.
Jack did the work **quickly enough** to finish half an hour early.

blocks.text: **Too** does not mean the same as **very**. We only use **too** when we are describing something negative.

blocks.correct: I've got **too much** work. I can't come out tonight.
blocks.incorrect: This job is great because you get paid **too much** money.

items: You're not **old enough** to work here.
You're not **enough old** to work here. ✗

blocks.intro: Both **too** and **enough** can be followed by **for**.
items: It's too hot **for me** in this office.
You're not old enough **for** the army.

items.prompt: The pan was ___ hot that I nearly dropped it!
Mr Jones was ___ a kind man that I was sad when he moved to another town.

exercises.title: B · Tick or correct
exercises.instruction: If the phrase in bold is correct, write the same phrase. If it is wrong, write the correct phrase.

items.prompt: Paris Hilton is **such famous** that she gets recognised wherever she goes.
There were **so many customers in the shop that** I couldn't move!
acceptedAnswers: so many customers in the shop that

items.prompt: The man spoke **such quickly** that I couldn't understand a word he said.
I had **so good marks** that my dad bought me a new computer!
Victoria is **so old that** she can remember seeing a car for the first time.

I've got **so a lot of friends** that I don't have time to see them all.
acceptedAnswers: such a lot of friends that

items.prompt: Big Brother was **such successful** that they're making another series.

exercises.title: C · Similar meaning
exercises.instruction: Complete each second sentence using the word given, so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence. Write between two and five words.

items.prompt:

I have ___ that I don't know what to do with it.
acceptedAnswers: such a lot of money that I don't know what to do with it.
such a lot of money that I don't know what to do with it

exercises.title: F · My first — and last! — day at work
exercises.instruction: Write so, such, too or enough in each gap.

items.prompt: I'll never forget my first day at work. It was (1) ___ a disaster that I lost my job!
The boss explained what I had to do, but she did it (2) ___ quickly that I didn't understand.
I wasn't brave (3) ___ to ask her to repeat it, so I pretended I knew what to do.
It wasn't difficult at first — just putting numbers into a computer. Soon, though, I was (4) ___ busy that I started making more and more mistakes.
I made (5) ___ a lot of mistakes that the other workers noticed.
They tried to help me, but it was (6) ___ late.
In the end, I just had (7) ___ much to do that I gave up.
I sat there and stared at my computer for two hours! The boss came back and she was (8) ___ shocked that she fired me immediately! My first day was also my last!
